observation: Residents and eligible property owners were consulted on parking changes following community feedback about parking availability. Support varied by street segment: 86%, 100%, 88% and 56%.
representativeness: Low geographic coverage; only eligible properties on specified street sections could participate. Not representative of the whole electorate.

observation: Development Victoria reports strong community support for redevelopment of the former VicRoads site and recognition of a need for more homes; feedback also sought better public spaces, walking/cycling links, green space and heritage recognition.
representativeness: Specific project consultation; participant count and response distribution not stated on summary page. Not an electorate-wide measure.

observation: The Kew MP raised reported resident concerns about dust, construction noise, amenity and changes to the local environment, including the design and performance of noise walls.
representativeness: A parliamentary statement reporting constituent concerns; no count or independent survey supplied.

observation: The Kew MP reported that residents were concerned about the planned removal of a city-bound bus stop near the Eastern Freeway entry ramp and raised the need for more frequent Route 200 services to Bulleen Park and Ride.
sentiment_target: bus stop removal and service frequency
representativeness: A parliamentary question reporting constituent concerns; no count or independent survey supplied.

geographic_scope: Barkers Road; Willsmere Road / Earl Street
observation: The Kew MP raised road-safety concerns and called for pedestrian crossings at Barkers Road and the Willsmere Road/Earl Street roundabout, citing near misses, injuries and petitions said to have attracted thousands of signatures.
representativeness: A parliamentary statement; petition totals and underlying responses should be independently verified before quantitative use.

geographic_scope: Boroondara LGA - contextual proxy not Kew electorate only
source_name: City of Boroondara - Community Plan consultation results
observation: Across the municipality, the survey's highest-ranked focus areas included green space, sport and recreation, personal safety/crime/policing, active travel, respect and inclusion, and rates/cost of council services. Workshop priorities differed, highlighting active travel, green space, housing affordability/diversity and preventing inappropriate development.
representativeness: More than 5,000 community survey participants and 156 workshop participants; municipality-wide, not electorate-specific.
